He borrowed a carbine from a sergeant, rested it on a fence rail, and fired at a distant Confederate officer. The shot missed — but 51,000 casualties would follow.

attrs.summary: When Gordon's Confederate brigade swept over Barlow's Knoll, General Francis Barlow was shot and left for dead among his fallen men. Confederate General John Gordon rode to the dying Union general, gave him water, tried to comfort him, and promised to find his wife. The two men met again after the war and became friends — one of the most remarkable reconciliation stories of the conflict.

Against direct orders, General Daniel Sickles advanced his entire III Corps nearly a mile forward from its assigned position on Cemetery Ridge to the Peach Orchard on the Emmitsburg Road. The move created a dangerously exposed salient. When Longstreet's assault struck it that afternoon, the salient collapsed in catastrophe — but Sickles would spend the rest of his long life arguing he had been right.

Colonel Hiram Berdan led his regiment of green-uniformed sharpshooters into Pitzer's Woods on a reconnaissance ordered by Sickles. They found Wilcox's Confederate infantry already positioned there — confirming Confederate activity on Seminary Ridge south of town. The reconnaissance gave Sickles his justification for advancing to the Peach Orchard.

With Little Round Top undefended and Confederate infantry racing to take it, General Warren intercepted Vincent's brigade on the march and redirected it up the hill. Vincent placed his regiments on the slope just minutes before Law's Confederates arrived. Colonel Strong Vincent was mortally wounded holding the position he had seized — he died a brigadier general, his promotion arriving while he lay dying.

After repulsing five Confederate assaults with nearly empty cartridge boxes, Colonel Joshua Chamberlain ordered the 20th Maine to fix bayonets and charge downhill. The attack swept the 15th Alabama from the slope and captured nearly 400 prisoners. It was the most celebrated regimental action of the battle — and possibly of the entire war.

Captain John Bigelow's 9th Massachusetts Battery was ordered to hold the Trostle Farm without infantry support — to buy time for McGilvery to form the artillery line that would stop the Confederate breakthrough. The battery fought its withdrawal by prolonge, losing men and guns but accomplishing its mission. A cannonball through the barn wall is still visible today.

attrs.location: Cemetery Ridge south, near Plum Run
attrs.summary: With Cemetery Ridge open and Wilcox's Confederate brigade advancing toward the gap, General Hancock turned to the only regiment near at hand — 262 men of the 1st Minnesota. He ordered them to charge an entire Confederate brigade to buy five minutes for reinforcements to arrive. They did it. 224 of 262 men fell. The regiment suffered the highest casualty rate of any Union regiment in a single engagement in the entire war.

attrs.summary: When the XII Corps was stripped from Culp's Hill to reinforce Cemetery Ridge, only George Greene's New York brigade remained — 1,424 men to hold the position against Johnson's entire Confederate division of 6,500. Greene extended his line impossibly thin and held for three hours. It was one of the finest defensive performances of the entire war.

At dusk on July 2, Hays's Louisiana Tigers and Avery's North Carolina brigade stormed Cemetery Hill in near-darkness. They reached the crest, seized Union artillery, and held it briefly — the closest any Confederate force came to breaking the Union center. Colonel Avery was mortally wounded on the slope, writing his last message in his own blood.

attrs.summary: As the Confederate cannonade approached its end, Colonel Edward Porter Alexander sent two messages to General Pickett that define the moment when the charge became inevitable. The first urged haste — ammunition was nearly gone. The second, the most ominous, told Pickett that Alexander himself would not advise making the charge — but that the order had been given and the troops were already moving.

Brigadier General Lewis Armistead placed his hat on his sword as a guide and led his brigade over the stone wall at The Angle — the deepest Confederate penetration of the battle. He was shot down moments later, falling among Union troops beyond the wall. His old friend Winfield Hancock was wounded simultaneously on the other side of the ridge. Both men lay bleeding at the High Water Mark of the Confederacy.

At approximately 1:00pm on July 3, two Confederate signal guns fired in sequence and 170 guns erupted along Seminary Ridge — the largest artillery bombardment ever seen on the North American continent. The sound was heard in Philadelphia, 140 miles away. Alexander's guns fired for nearly two hours before Pickett stepped off.

Lieutenant Alonzo Cushing served his last two guns at The Angle through the Confederate cannonade and Pickett's assault, twice wounded but refusing to leave. He was killed while firing at Armistead's men crossing the wall — shot through the mouth. He received the Medal of Honor in 2014, 151 years after his death — the longest gap between action and award in the history of the decoration.

After the repulse of Pickett's Charge, Lee rode forward to meet his broken men and told them repeatedly: 'It is all my fault.' General Pickett, asked by Lee to reform his division for defense, replied: 'General Lee, I have no division.' Pickett never forgave Lee for ordering the charge and never recovered from the loss of his men.

Three miles east of Gettysburg, while Pickett's infantry was being repulsed at The Angle, Stuart's cavalry attempted to sweep around the Union rear. The 23-year-old General George Armstrong Custer personally led the Michigan Brigade in a mounted charge that stopped Stuart cold. 'Come on, you Wolverines!' he shouted — and they came.

General Elon Farnsworth had been a general for eight days when Kilpatrick ordered him to charge Confederate infantry over rocky terrain south of the battlefield. Farnsworth protested that the charge was suicidal. Kilpatrick insisted. Farnsworth led the charge and was killed. He had been a general for exactly four days when he died.

records.title: Iron Brigade crashes into Archer's Confederate brigade in Herbst Woods.

attrs.text: Iron Brigade sweeps through Herbst Woods. Archer's brigade broken and fleeing west across Willoughby Run. I Corps establishes defensive line along McPherson's Ridge south of Chambersburg Pike.

records.label: Iron Brigade sweeps through Herbst Woods.
records.title: Iron Brigade sweeps through Herbst Woods.

attrs.text: North of the pike, Davis's Confederate brigade advances in three regiments. Cutler's Union brigade rushes to deploy north of Chambersburg Pike. Hall's battery (2nd Maine) unlimbers in the Railroad Cut area.

records.label: North of the pike, Davis's Confederate brigade advances in three regiments.
records.title: North of the pike, Davis's Confederate brigade advances in three regiments.

attrs.text: Davis's brigade overlaps Cutler's right flank. 76th NY and 56th PA take heavy fire and are forced back. 147th NY stands alone briefly. Meredith wounded — Robinson assumes Iron Brigade command.

records.label: Davis's brigade overlaps Cutler's right flank.
records.title: Davis's brigade overlaps Cutler's right flank.

attrs.text: Davis's brigade pursues Cutler north. 2nd Mississippi and 42nd Mississippi enter the unfinished Railroad Cut west of the pike. Hall's battery forced to withdraw under Confederate pressure.
6th Wisconsin (Dawes) detached from Iron Brigade and ordered north across the pike. Joins 14th Brooklyn and 95th NY. Dawes orders charge directly at the Railroad Cut.

records.label: 6th Wisconsin (Dawes) detached from Iron Brigade and ordered north across the pike.
records.title: 6th Wisconsin (Dawes) detached from Iron Brigade and ordered north across the pike.

attrs.text: 6th Wisconsin reaches the cut. Davis's Confederates trapped — the cut at the middle position is 15 feet deep and impossible to climb under fire. Mass surrender. Dawes demands surrender: 'Where is the colonel of this regiment?' 232 Confederates captured.

attrs.narrative: The 'noon lull' lasted roughly 10:30am-1:00pm. Both sides used the pause to bring up reinforcements and reorganize.
attrs.text: Noon lull begins. Both sides reorganize. Confederate Heth, finding the resistance much heavier than expected, halts and waits for Rodes and Early to arrive from the north. Reynolds replacement confirmed as Doubleday.

I Corps completing deployment on McPherson's Ridge and Seminary Ridge. Robinson's division (2nd Division) arrives and takes position on Oak Ridge north of the pike. Buford's cavalry screens the flanks.

records.label: I Corps completing deployment on McPherson's Ridge and Seminary Ridge.
records.title: I Corps completing deployment on McPherson's Ridge and Seminary Ridge.

attrs.narrative: Rodes's arrival at Oak Hill was an accidental tactical gift — he could see the exposed Union right flank from the hill.
attrs.text: Rodes's Confederate division (Second Corps) arrives on Oak Hill north of Gettysburg. Rodes sees the Union I Corps position from Oak Hill. Recognizes he can attack the I Corps right flank. Begins deploying.

records.label: Rodes's Confederate division (Second Corps) arrives on Oak Hill north of Gettysburg.
records.title: Rodes's Confederate division (Second Corps) arrives on Oak Hill north of Gettysburg.

attrs.text: Confederate artillery (Jones's and Andrews's battalions) deploys on Oak Hill. Carrington's and Carter's batteries open fire on Union I Corps from an enfilading position — devastating flanking fire.

records.label: Confederate artillery (Jones's and Andrews's battalions) deploys on Oak Hill.
records.title: Confederate artillery (Jones's and Andrews's battalions) deploys on Oak Hill.

attrs.text: XI Corps (Howard) begins arriving north of Gettysburg. Howard takes overall command as senior officer. Schurz's division deploys north of town. Barlow's division pushes to Blocher's Knoll (Barlow's Knoll) against Howard's orders.

records.label: XI Corps (Howard) begins arriving north of Gettysburg.
records.title: XI Corps (Howard) begins arriving north of Gettysburg.

attrs.text: Rodes attacks. O'Neal's brigade miscarries — O'Neal does not lead in person, keeps one regiment back without orders. Iverson's brigade advances in PERFECT ALIGNMENT without skirmishers toward Oak Ridge stone wall.

IVERSON'S PITS. Baxter's Union brigade (behind stone wall) fires simultaneous volley into Iverson's flank at close range. Approximately 500 Confederates shot down in minutes. Men fall in rows — their graves visible as depressions today. Iverson reportedly does not lead the charge.
Daniel's Confederate brigade attacks south of Iverson toward the Railroad Cut area. Ramseur's brigade waits to exploit any opening. O'Neal's repulsed regiments reorganize.

records.label: Daniel's Confederate brigade attacks south of Iverson toward the Railroad Cut area.
records.title: Daniel's Confederate brigade attacks south of Iverson toward the Railroad Cut area.

attrs.text: GORDON'S FLANK ATTACK. Early's division arrives on York Road northeast of town. Gordon's brigade sweeps wide around the Union XI Corps right flank, hitting Barlow's position on Barlow's Knoll from the east. Doles's brigade simultaneously attacks north of town.

Barlow's Knoll overwhelmed. Barlow severely wounded — left for dead on the knoll. Gordon personally brings him water, believing him dying. Wilkeson's Union battery destroyed on the knoll. Hays's and Avery's brigades advance south toward town.
XI Corps collapses. Barlow's and Schurz's divisions broken and streaming south through Gettysburg streets. Coster's brigade sent north to cover the retreat — trapped in the brickyard disaster.
Coster's brigade caught from three sides in brickyard north of town — 566 casualties in minutes. 134th NY, 154th NY, 27th PA, 73rd PA nearly destroyed as organized units.

records.label: Coster's brigade caught from three sides in brickyard north of town — 566 casualties in minutes.
records.title: Coster's brigade caught from three sides in brickyard north of town — 566 casualties in minutes.

attrs.text: I Corps right flank (Robinson) crumbling under Oak Hill artillery and Daniel's brigade pressure. Paul's brigade commander Paul blinded — four successive commanders wounded. 16th Maine ordered to stay as sacrifice regiment covering the retreat.

records.label: I Corps right flank (Robinson) crumbling under Oak Hill artillery and Daniel's brigade pressure.
records.title: I Corps right flank (Robinson) crumbling under Oak Hill artillery and Daniel's brigade pressure.

attrs.text: Seminary Ridge fighting begins. Pender's Confederate division arrives and attacks I Corps position. Perrin's South Carolina brigade drives through the Lutheran Seminary grounds. Scales's brigade devastated — 66% casualties.
Schimmelfennig cut off during retreat — hides in a pigpen on Baltimore Street. Von Amsberg assumes XI Corps brigade command. I Corps remnants retreating through town.

records.label: Schimmelfennig cut off during retreat — hides in a pigpen on Baltimore Street.
records.title: Schimmelfennig cut off during retreat — hides in a pigpen on Baltimore Street.

attrs.text: Dilger's battery (Battery I, 1st Ohio) fights rearguard action THROUGH GETTYSBURG'S STREETS — the only artillery to fight in the town itself. Engages Confederate infantry at close range on Stratton Street and Washington Street.

records.label: Dilger's battery (Battery I, 1st Ohio) fights rearguard action THROUGH GETTYSBURG'S STREETS…
records.title: Dilger's battery (Battery I, 1st Ohio) fights rearguard action THROUGH GETTYSBURG'S STREETS…

attrs.narrative: Hancock's energy and presence stabilized the Union position when everything seemed lost.
attrs.text: Union forces rally on Cemetery Hill. Howard had wisely positioned a reserve (von Steinwehr's division) here from the start. Hancock arrives from Meade — takes command and organizes the defense.

records.label: Union forces rally on Cemetery Hill.
records.title: Union forces rally on Cemetery Hill.

attrs.narrative: Ewell's decision not to attack Cemetery Hill July 1 evening is one of the most debated command decisions of the war. Jackson would likely have attacked.
attrs.text: LEE'S DISCRETIONARY ORDER TO EWELL: 'take Cemetery Hill if practicable.' Ewell looks at the hill, considers Johnson's division not yet arrived, decides it is not practicable. Does not order the attack.
Johnson's Confederate division arrives on the Hanover Road. Positions east of Gettysburg. Faces Culp's Hill. Ewell places his corps in a line stretching from Culp's Hill to north of town.

records.label: Johnson's Confederate division arrives on the Hanover Road.
records.title: Johnson's Confederate division arrives on the Hanover Road.

attrs.text: XII Corps (Williams) arrives on Baltimore Pike and takes position on Culp's Hill. Greene's brigade on the right. Powers Hill reserve. XII Corps secures the Union right flank.

records.label: XII Corps (Williams) arrives on Baltimore Pike and takes position on Culp's Hill.
records.title: XII Corps (Williams) arrives on Baltimore Pike and takes position on Culp's Hill.

attrs.text: Meade replaces Doubleday with Newton to command I Corps. II Corps (Hancock) begins arriving and extending the Union line south on Cemetery Ridge. Birney's III Corps division arrives.

records.label: Meade replaces Doubleday with Newton to command I Corps.
records.title: Meade replaces Doubleday with Newton to command I Corps.

attrs.narrative: The fish-hook defensive line the Union occupied at the end of July 1 was one of the strongest defensive positions of the war.
attrs.text: By nightfall the Union Army holds the fish-hook line: Cemetery Hill, Cemetery Ridge, Culp's Hill. Meade arrives in person at ~11pm. Holds council of war — decides to stay and fight. Confederate army holds Seminary Ridge and the town.

records.label: By nightfall the Union Army holds the fish-hook line: Cemetery Hill, Cemetery Ridge, Culp's…
records.title: By nightfall the Union Army holds the fish-hook line: Cemetery Hill, Cemetery Ridge, Culp's…

attrs.narrative: Lee's decision to attack on July 2 rather than maneuver is the second most-debated Confederate command decision of the battle.
attrs.text: Both armies consolidate overnight positions. Lee reconnoiters the Union line from Seminary Ridge. Longstreet argues again for a strategic flanking movement. Lee overrules — orders Longstreet to attack the Union left. The attack is to begin as early as possible.

Sickles examines his assigned position on lower Cemetery Ridge and is dissatisfied. He believes the Peach Orchard ridge is higher ground and would be better. He begins to consider an unauthorized advance.

records.label: Sickles examines his assigned position on lower Cemetery Ridge and is dissatisfied.
records.title: Sickles examines his assigned position on lower Cemetery Ridge and is dissatisfied.

attrs.text: Longstreet's corps begins moving south for the flanking march. The march is complicated by the need to avoid Union observation from Little Round Top. Longstreet is slow and deliberate — the controversial delay begins.

records.label: Longstreet's corps begins moving south for the flanking march.
records.title: Longstreet's corps begins moving south for the flanking march.

attrs.text: Berdan's sharpshooters (1st US Sharpshooters) sent into Pitzer's Woods by Sickles for reconnaissance. They find Wilcox's Confederate infantry. This confirms Confederate presence on Seminary Ridge south of town.

records.label: Berdan's sharpshooters (1st US Sharpshooters) sent into Pitzer's Woods by Sickles for…
records.title: Berdan's sharpshooters (1st US Sharpshooters) sent into Pitzer's Woods by Sickles for…

attrs.location: Warfield Ridge / south of Peach Orchard
attrs.text: Hood's division completes the flanking march and deploys south of Gettysburg. McLaws deploys north of Hood along Warfield Ridge. Alexander positions his artillery. The assault force is in position.

records.label: Hood's division completes the flanking march and deploys south of Gettysburg.
records.place: Warfield Ridge / south of Peach Orchard
records.title: Hood's division completes the flanking march and deploys south of Gettysburg.

attrs.narrative: Sickles's unauthorized advance was tactically disastrous but may have drawn Confederate attention away from the Round Tops.
attrs.text: Sickles advances his entire III Corps to the Peach Orchard — without orders, without informing Meade, without permission. Creates a salient with an exposed apex at the Orchard and a dangerously thin line stretching to Devil's Den.

records.label: Sickles advances his entire III Corps to the Peach Orchard — without orders, without…
records.title: Sickles advances his entire III Corps to the Peach Orchard — without orders, without…

attrs.text: Meade discovers Sickles's unauthorized advance. Furious confrontation. Meade orders Sickles back — but Confederate artillery has already opened fire and it is too late to withdraw without chaos.

LONGSTREET'S ASSAULT BEGINS. Alexander's Confederate artillery opens fire on the Peach Orchard salient — 54 guns. Hood's division steps off in Line of Battle heading northeast toward Devil's Den and the Round Tops.
Hood severely wounded — arm permanently paralyzed by artillery fragment. Law assumes division command. Hood's request to swing around Big Round Top is denied by Longstreet.

records.label: Hood severely wounded — arm permanently paralyzed by artillery fragment.
records.title: Hood severely wounded — arm permanently paralyzed by artillery fragment.

attrs.location: Devil's Den / Little Round Top south slope
attrs.text: Law's brigade (formerly Hood's) reaches Big Round Top. 15th Alabama turns left and begins assaulting the southern slope of Little Round Top. Robertson's Texas Brigade engages Ward's Union brigade at Devil's Den and the Triangular Field.

records.label: Law's brigade (formerly Hood's) reaches Big Round Top.
records.place: Devil's Den / Little Round Top south slope
records.title: Law's brigade (formerly Hood's) reaches Big Round Top.

attrs.narrative: Warren's recognition of the Little Round Top crisis and his desperate improvisation to fill it was one of the most consequential individual decisions of the battle.
attrs.text: Little Round Top is UNOCCUPIED by Union infantry — only a signal station on the summit. Warren, Meade's chief engineer, realizes the danger and desperately searches for troops to send there.

records.label: Little Round Top is UNOCCUPIED by Union infantry — only a signal station on the summit.
records.title: Little Round Top is UNOCCUPIED by Union infantry — only a signal station on the summit.

attrs.text: Warren intercepts Vincent's brigade (V Corps) on the march and diverts it to Little Round Top without waiting for formal orders. Vincent personally leads the brigade up the hill.

records.label: Warren intercepts Vincent's brigade (V Corps) on the march and diverts it to Little Round…
records.title: Warren intercepts Vincent's brigade (V Corps) on the march and diverts it to Little Round…

attrs.text: Vincent's brigade arrives on Little Round Top just ahead of Law's Confederates. Vincent places his regiments on the rocky slope: 16th Michigan right, 44th NY center, 83rd PA center-left, 20th Maine on the extreme left.

records.label: Vincent's brigade arrives on Little Round Top just ahead of Law's Confederates.
records.title: Vincent's brigade arrives on Little Round Top just ahead of Law's Confederates.

attrs.text: 15th Alabama (Oates) makes its first assault on 20th Maine's refused left flank. Chamberlain's line bends but holds. Multiple Confederate assaults follow over the next 30-40 minutes.

records.label: 15th Alabama (Oates) makes its first assault on 20th Maine's refused left flank.
records.title: 15th Alabama (Oates) makes its first assault on 20th Maine's refused left flank.

attrs.text: Vincent mortally wounded on Little Round Top. Rice assumes brigade command. Weed's brigade arrives on the summit. Hazlett drags guns up the steep rocky slope. O'Rorke's 140th NY arrives at the summit.

records.label: Vincent mortally wounded on Little Round Top.
records.title: Vincent mortally wounded on Little Round Top.

attrs.text: O'Rorke charges downhill without waiting for orders — 140th NY sweeps Confederates off the northern slope of Little Round Top. O'Rorke shot through the neck and killed instantly.

records.label: O'Rorke charges downhill without waiting for orders — 140th NY sweeps Confederates off the…
records.title: O'Rorke charges downhill without waiting for orders — 140th NY sweeps Confederates off the…

attrs.text: Weed killed on the summit. Hazlett shot kneeling beside the dying Weed. Both general and artillery commander die almost simultaneously. Rittenhouse assumes battery command.
16th Michigan on Vincent's right begins to waver — brief near-break. The regiment steadies before the line collapses. Critical moment.

records.label: 16th Michigan on Vincent's right begins to waver — brief near-break.
records.title: 16th Michigan on Vincent's right begins to waver — brief near-break.

attrs.text: CHAMBERLAIN'S BAYONET CHARGE. 20th Maine has expended nearly all ammunition after repulsing multiple assaults. Chamberlain orders a bayonet charge — right-wheel motion sweeping down the hill. 15th Alabama broken and retreating. Nearly 400 Confederate prisoners.
McLaws's assault begins. Barksdale's Mississippi brigade charges the Peach Orchard in one of the most dramatic charges of the battle. Barksdale rides ahead of his men on horseback.
Peach Orchard salient collapses. Graham wounded and captured. 141st PA suffers 71% casualties at the apex. III Corps line crumbling from the south toward Cemetery Ridge.
Kershaw's South Carolina brigade engages in Rose Woods and the Wheatfield. DeTrobriand's Union brigade holds initially. G.T. Anderson's Georgia brigade pressing from the south.

records.label: Kershaw's South Carolina brigade engages in Rose Woods and the Wheatfield.
records.title: Kershaw's South Carolina brigade engages in Rose Woods and the Wheatfield.

attrs.narrative: Father Corby administers general absolution to the Irish Brigade before the charge. A kneeling army watches from Cemetery Ridge.
attrs.text: Caldwell's II Corps division rushed south to reinforce the collapsing III Corps. Four brigades — Cross, Kelly (Irish Brigade), Zook, Brooke — advance into the Wheatfield.

records.label: Caldwell's II Corps division rushed south to reinforce the collapsing III Corps.
records.title: Caldwell's II Corps division rushed south to reinforce the collapsing III Corps.

attrs.narrative: Corby stood on a rock and gave absolution — all nearby troops of any faith knelt or bowed their heads.
attrs.text: Father Corby's absolution. The Irish Brigade kneels in the field to receive general absolution before charging into the Wheatfield. One of the most dramatic religious moments of the war.
Cross killed entering the Wheatfield. Zook mortally wounded. Brooke's brigade pushes farthest into the Wheatfield of any Union brigade. Semmes's Confederates mortally wounded.

Wofford's fresh Georgia brigade sweeps through the Wheatfield behind the retreating Caldwell — reaches the farthest Confederate penetration toward Cemetery Ridge. Tilton's controversial withdrawal exposed the Union flank.

records.label: Wofford's fresh Georgia brigade sweeps through the Wheatfield behind the retreating Caldwell…
records.title: Wofford's fresh Georgia brigade sweeps through the Wheatfield behind the retreating Caldwell…

attrs.location: Wheatfield / Little Round Top west slope
attrs.text: Crawford's Pennsylvania Reserves charge down the western slope of Little Round Top — drives Wofford's exhausted Confederates back through the Wheatfield. Colonel Taylor of 13th PA Reserves killed. Caldwell's position partially restored.

records.label: Crawford's Pennsylvania Reserves charge down the western slope of Little Round Top — drives…
records.place: Wheatfield / Little Round Top west slope
records.title: Crawford's Pennsylvania Reserves charge down the western slope of Little Round Top — drives…

attrs.text: SICKLES WOUNDED. Artillery shell shatters Sickles's right leg near the Trostle Farm. Sickles famously smokes a cigar as he is carried from the field. Birney assumes III Corps command.

McGilvery's emergency artillery line. McGilvery assembles guns from multiple batteries — Bigelow, Phillips, Hart — along Plum Run to plug the gap left by III Corps collapse. Bigelow's battery ordered to hold without support.

BIGELOW'S TROSTLE FARM WITHDRAWAL. Bigelow's 9th Massachusetts battery ordered to hold as long as possible to buy time for McGilvery. Battery fights by prolonge (rope), losing guns one by one. Heroic withdrawal saves McGilvery's line.

1ST MINNESOTA'S CHARGE. Cemetery Ridge gap is open. Wilcox's Confederate brigade advancing toward the gap. Hancock has nothing to send but Colvill's 262-man 1st Minnesota. 'My God, are these all the men we have?' Orders them to charge Wilcox's entire brigade to buy 5 minutes.

1st Minnesota engages Wilcox's Confederate brigade. Both flanks overlapped but the charge stops Wilcox long enough for reinforcements to arrive. Colvill wounded, Messick killed, Coates assumes command. 85.5% casualties.
Wilcox's advance halted. Reinforcements close the gap on Cemetery Ridge. Wright's Georgia brigade briefly breaks through Cemetery Ridge north of Wilcox but is driven back without support.

Stuart arrives with his cavalry after controversial absence. Lee reportedly greets him: 'General Stuart, where have you been?' Confederate cavalry now available for the first time since before the campaign began.

records.label: Stuart arrives with his cavalry after controversial absence.
records.title: Stuart arrives with his cavalry after controversial absence.

attrs.narrative: Greene's lone stand is one of the finest defensive performances of the war — 1,424 men holding against 6,500.
attrs.text: Johnson's Confederate division advances on Culp's Hill at dusk. XII Corps has been stripped away to reinforce Cemetery Ridge leaving only Greene's brigade (1,424 men) to hold the entire hill against 6,500 Confederates.

records.label: Johnson's Confederate division advances on Culp's Hill at dusk.
records.title: Johnson's Confederate division advances on Culp's Hill at dusk.

attrs.text: GREENE'S LONE STAND. Greene's brigade holds Culp's Hill alone. Johnson's Confederates (Stonewall Brigade, Jones, Nicholls, Steuart) assault repeatedly. Greene extends his thin line and bends but never breaks.

Steuart's Confederate brigade occupies vacant XII Corps breastworks on lower Culp's Hill — the right of the Union position. XII Corps (returning from Cemetery Ridge) finds their own works occupied by Confederates.

records.label: Steuart's Confederate brigade occupies vacant XII Corps breastworks on lower Culp's Hill —…
records.title: Steuart's Confederate brigade occupies vacant XII Corps breastworks on lower Culp's Hill —…

attrs.text: XII Corps returns to Culp's Hill and finds Confederate troops in their works. Night attack repossesses most of the upper works. Lower works remain Confederate. Sets up the July 3 morning fight.

records.label: XII Corps returns to Culp's Hill and finds Confederate troops in their works.
records.title: XII Corps returns to Culp's Hill and finds Confederate troops in their works.

attrs.text: CEMETERY HILL ASSAULT. Hays's Louisiana Tigers and Avery's North Carolina brigade charge Cemetery Hill at dusk. They reach the crest and briefly seize Union guns.
Avery mortally wounded on the slope of Cemetery Hill writing his blood message: 'Tell my father I died with my face to the enemy.' Godwin assumes brigade command.

records.label: Avery mortally wounded on the slope of Cemetery Hill writing his blood message: 'Tell my…
records.title: Avery mortally wounded on the slope of Cemetery Hill writing his blood message: 'Tell my…

attrs.text: Carroll's Union brigade counterattacks Cemetery Hill — drives Louisiana Tigers and Avery's brigade back down the slope. Cemetery Hill secure. The last Confederate attempt to take the Union center ends.

records.label: Carroll's Union brigade counterattacks Cemetery Hill — drives Louisiana Tigers and Avery's…
records.title: Carroll's Union brigade counterattacks Cemetery Hill — drives Louisiana Tigers and Avery's…

attrs.text: Willard's brigade (II Corps — 'Harper's Ferry Cowards' seeking redemption) charges Barksdale's exhausted Confederates near Plum Run. Willard killed by artillery shell. Barksdale mortally wounded nearby. Both commanders fall almost simultaneously.

records.label: Willard's brigade (II Corps — 'Harper's Ferry Cowards' seeking redemption) charges…
records.title: Willard's brigade (II Corps — 'Harper's Ferry Cowards' seeking redemption) charges…

attrs.narrative: July 2 was the bloodiest single day of the Gettysburg campaign — approximately 20,000 total casualties across both armies.
attrs.text: Fighting dies down across the battlefield. Both sides hold approximately their morning positions except: Confederates hold lower Culp's Hill works. Union line on Cemetery Ridge is intact. III Corps is shattered. The enormous cost of July 2 becomes clear.

records.label: Fighting dies down across the battlefield.
records.title: Fighting dies down across the battlefield.

attrs.narrative: This exchange — Longstreet's most famous protest — became the center of the Lost Cause argument that Longstreet lost Gettysburg. Most historians side with Longstreet's assessment.
attrs.text: Lee and Longstreet meet. Lee decides to attack Cemetery Ridge with Pickett's fresh division plus Pettigrew and Trimble July 3. Longstreet argues against it: 'General, I have been a soldier all my life... it is my opinion that no 15,000 men ever arrayed for battle can take that position.' Lee overrules.
Alexander begins positioning Confederate artillery along Seminary Ridge for the July 3 cannonade. Approximately 170 guns will fire tomorrow. The ammunition situation is already tight.

records.label: Alexander begins positioning Confederate artillery along Seminary Ridge for the July 3…
records.title: Alexander begins positioning Confederate artillery along Seminary Ridge for the July 3…

attrs.narrative: Meade's prediction that Lee would attack his center on July 3 is one of the most accurate command predictions of the war.
attrs.text: Meade holds council of war. All corps commanders polled — decision is unanimous to remain and fight on July 3. Meade predicts Lee will attack his center. He is correct.
Both armies settle in for the night. Pickett's division — fresh, not yet engaged — moves into position behind Seminary Ridge. Pettigrew's and Trimble's commands positioned on Seminary Ridge left.

records.label: Both armies settle in for the night.
records.title: Both armies settle in for the night.

attrs.text: Johnson's Confederates dig in on lower Culp's Hill. XII Corps prepares for the morning counterattack. Meade orders artillery chief Hunt to conserve ammunition — critical decision for July 3.

records.label: Johnson's Confederates dig in on lower Culp's Hill.
records.title: Johnson's Confederates dig in on lower Culp's Hill.

attrs.text: End of Day 2. Tallying casualties: approximately 10,000 Union, 10,000 Confederate. III Corps effectively destroyed as a fighting force. Both Round Tops firmly in Union hands. Cemetery Hill and Culp's Hill (mostly) held. Lee will attack the center tomorrow.

Day 3 opens with Union XII Corps artillery firing on Johnson's Confederates dug into the lower Culp's Hill breastworks. The bombardment opens the longest sustained infantry fight of the battle — seven hours.

records.label: Day 3 opens with Union XII Corps artillery firing on Johnson's Confederates dug into the…
records.title: Day 3 opens with Union XII Corps artillery firing on Johnson's Confederates dug into the…

attrs.text: Johnson's Confederate division counterattacks to retain the breastworks. Stonewall Brigade, Jones, Nicholls, Steuart assault the XII Corps line. Greene's brigade and returning XII Corps units resist along the hillside works.

records.label: Johnson's Confederate division counterattacks to retain the breastworks.
records.title: Johnson's Confederate division counterattacks to retain the breastworks.

attrs.text: Steuart's Confederate brigade makes repeated assaults up the steep hill. 1st Maryland Confederate and 3rd NC suffer heavy casualties. The parallel fight between Union and Confederate Maryland regiments is ongoing here.

records.label: Steuart's Confederate brigade makes repeated assaults up the steep hill.
records.title: Steuart's Confederate brigade makes repeated assaults up the steep hill.

attrs.text: Colgrove's controversial charge. Mudge's 2nd Massachusetts and 27th Indiana ordered to charge across an open meadow toward Confederate positions. Mudge's last words: 'It is murder but it is the order.' Mudge killed leading the charge.
Both sides fight a grinding attritional battle on Culp's Hill. Johnson's Confederates make twelve distinct assaults. XII Corps holds the upper works throughout. Confederate ammunition running low.

records.label: Both sides fight a grinding attritional battle on Culp's Hill.
records.title: Both sides fight a grinding attritional battle on Culp's Hill.

attrs.text: XII Corps counterattacks aggressively. Candy's, Kane's, and Greene's brigades advance to recapture lower works. Johnson's division slowly pushed back. Steuart's brigade suffering severely.
Johnson's Confederate assault on Culp's Hill exhausted. Confederate ammunition nearly expended. Johnson signals Ewell that he cannot continue. Ewell orders Johnson to hold what he has.

records.label: Johnson's Confederate assault on Culp's Hill exhausted.
records.title: Johnson's Confederate assault on Culp's Hill exhausted.

attrs.text: Pickett's fresh division moves up behind Seminary Ridge in preparation for the afternoon assault. The three Virginia brigades (Garnett, Kemper, Armistead) form in the woods, invisible to Union observers.

records.label: Pickett's fresh division moves up behind Seminary Ridge in preparation for the afternoon…
records.title: Pickett's fresh division moves up behind Seminary Ridge in preparation for the afternoon…

attrs.text: Pettigrew's division (Heth's old command) and Trimble's two brigades (Lane and Scales/Lowrance) positioned on Seminary Ridge left of Pickett. The assault force numbers approximately 12,500 men across a mile front.

records.label: Pettigrew's division (Heth's old command) and Trimble's two brigades (Lane and…
records.title: Pettigrew's division (Heth's old command) and Trimble's two brigades (Lane and…

attrs.text: Final Culp's Hill fighting. XII Corps retakes most of the contested works. Johnson's remaining Confederates hold a small section of the lower works but are effectively contained.

attrs.narrative: The seven-hour Culp's Hill fight was the longest sustained infantry battle of Gettysburg but is overshadowed by Pickett's Charge in popular memory.
attrs.text: Culp's Hill fighting finally ends at approximately 11:00am. Johnson's division retires. Twelve Confederate assaults repulsed. Union line on Culp's Hill completely restored. Total Culp's Hill casualties: approximately 3,500 across both days.

records.label: Culp's Hill fighting finally ends at approximately 11:00am.
records.title: Culp's Hill fighting finally ends at approximately 11:00am.

attrs.text: Alexander positions the Confederate artillery along Seminary Ridge for the cannonade. 170 Confederate guns arranged in a two-mile arc from the Peach Orchard north to the Hagerstown Road. Alexander writes two famous messages to Pickett.

records.label: Alexander positions the Confederate artillery along Seminary Ridge for the cannonade.
records.title: Alexander positions the Confederate artillery along Seminary Ridge for the cannonade.

attrs.narrative: Alexander later wrote that the cannonade was the most magnificent spectacle he ever witnessed. The Union artillery chief Hunt deliberately slowed Union counter-fire to conserve ammunition.
attrs.text: THE CANNONADE BEGINS. At approximately 1:00pm, two Confederate signal guns fire in sequence. 170 Confederate guns open fire simultaneously — the largest artillery bombardment in the history of the Western Hemisphere to that date. The sound is heard in Philadelphia, 140 miles away.

attrs.narrative: Hunt's decision to conserve ammunition was tactically correct. Hancock's decision to keep firing boosted infantry morale but depleted artillery reserves.
attrs.text: Hunt deliberately silences Union artillery to conserve ammunition for the infantry assault. Hancock overrules Hunt and orders the guns to keep firing for morale. The disagreement between Hunt and Hancock shapes the eventual repulse.

records.label: Hunt deliberately silences Union artillery to conserve ammunition for the infantry assault.
records.title: Hunt deliberately silences Union artillery to conserve ammunition for the infantry assault.

attrs.narrative: The Confederate tendency to overshoot was a significant tactical failure — the cannonade inflicted far less damage on the Union infantry than Lee and Alexander had hoped.
attrs.text: Confederate artillery fire overshooting Cemetery Ridge — most shells landing behind the Union line near Taneytown Road. Union artillery casualties lighter than expected. Meade's headquarters nearly hit.

records.label: Confederate artillery fire overshooting Cemetery Ridge — most shells landing behind the…
records.title: Confederate artillery fire overshooting Cemetery Ridge — most shells landing behind the…

attrs.narrative: Longstreet later wrote: 'I could not speak. I bowed in answer.' His reluctance to order the charge is evident in every account.
attrs.text: Alexander's first message to Pickett: 'For God's sake come quick or we cannot support you — ammunition nearly exhausted.' Pickett shows it to Longstreet. Longstreet cannot speak — nods his head. The charge is set in motion.

records.label: Alexander's first message to Pickett: 'For God's sake come quick or we cannot support you —…

attrs.text: Alexander's second message to Pickett: 'I would not make the charge now — but the order has been given and the troops are already moving.' Pickett's division steps out of the woods.

attrs.text: Stannard's Vermont Brigade (I Corps) takes position south of The Angle on Cemetery Ridge. Stannard has a clear view of Kemper's right flank. He is already planning the flanking maneuver.

attrs.text: PICKETT'S CHARGE BEGINS. The entire Confederate assault force — approximately 12,500 men in a mile-wide front — steps off Seminary Ridge in Line of Battle heading east across the open fields toward Cemetery Ridge. The most famous infantry assault in American history.
Union artillery opens with solid shot then shell as the Confederate line advances across the open ground. Each discharge tears gaps in the Confederate line. The attackers close ranks and keep moving.

attrs.text: BROCKENBROUGH COLLAPSES. The far Confederate left (Brockenbrough's Virginia brigade) breaks and retreats under flanking fire from the 8th Ohio's advanced skirmish position. Pettigrew's left flank is now exposed.

Confederate assault line reaches the Emmitsburg Road and crosses the fencing. Heavy casualties from Union artillery and musketry. Kemper's brigade begins obliquing left toward the Copse of Trees — exposing its right flank.

records.title: Confederate assault line reaches the Emmitsburg Road and crosses the fencing.

attrs.text: STANNARD'S FLANKING ATTACK. Stannard's Vermont brigade wheels left 90 degrees and pours enfilade fire into Kemper's exposed right flank. The 13th and 14th Vermont fire into the Confederate right. Kemper's brigade takes devastating flank fire.
Kemper severely wounded in the Confederate assault. Mayo assumes brigade command. Kemper briefly captured, then rescued by his men.

attrs.text: Pettigrew's Confederate brigades (26th NC, 11th NC, 47th NC, 52nd NC) reach the stone wall on Cemetery Ridge north of The Angle. Union II Corps (Smyth, Hays) fires at close range. 12th NJ fires buck-and-ball at point-blank range.

attrs.text: Garnett's Confederate brigade reaches the stone wall at The Angle. Heavy casualties from canister. Garnett rides on horseback (too ill to walk) — conspicuous and exposed. The two lines exchange fire at close range across the wall.

records.label: Garnett's Confederate brigade reaches the stone wall at The Angle.
records.title: Garnett's Confederate brigade reaches the stone wall at The Angle.

attrs.text: GARNETT KIA. Shot from his horse at The Angle — his body never officially identified after the battle. Marshall killed leading Pettigrew's brigade. Multiple Confederate commanders fall almost simultaneously.

aliases: ARMISTEAD LEADS MEN OVER THE WALL

attrs.text: ARMISTEAD LEADS MEN OVER THE WALL. Armistead places his hat on his sword as a guide and leads his brigade over the stone wall at The Angle — the deepest Confederate penetration of the battle. Approximately 150-200 men cross with him.

records.label: Armistead Leads Men Over The Wall
records.title: Armistead Leads Men Over The Wall

attrs.text: ARMISTEAD MORTALLY WOUNDED. Shot moments after crossing the wall — while touching a Union gun with his hand. Falls beyond the stone wall among Union troops. Armistead asks for Hancock to be brought to him. Hancock also wounded at this moment.
CUSHING KIA. Lieutenant Cushing, serving his last two guns at The Angle, shot through the mouth and killed. Sergeant Fuger assumes command of the shattered battery.

Cowan's Union battery fires canister into Armistead's men at approximately 50 yards — devastating close-range fire. Union infantry closes from multiple directions. The Confederate penetration is contained and then driven back.

records.label: Cowan's Union battery fires canister into Armistead's men at approximately 50 yards —…
records.title: Cowan's Union battery fires canister into Armistead's men at approximately 50 yards —…

attrs.text: The Confederate penetration is broken. Armistead's men streaming back over the wall or surrendering. Devereux's 19th Massachusetts and others pour into the breach. The Angle is secured.

attrs.narrative: Lee's acknowledgment — 'It is all my fault' — is one of the most famous statements of the war. He met his broken men personally and attempted to rally them for a Union counterattack that never came.
attrs.text: Along the entire line the Confederate assault collapses. Pettigrew's brigades fall back. Trimble (wounded) orders retreat. The survivors stream back toward Seminary Ridge. Lee rides forward to meet them: 'It is all my fault.'

records.label: Along the entire line the Confederate assault collapses.
records.title: Along the entire line the Confederate assault collapses.

attrs.text: 16TH VERMONT SECOND WHEEL. Stannard's 16th VT wheels again — now against Wilcox's and Lang's Confederate brigades advancing in belated support of Pickett. The double enfilade effectively seals the repulse on the south end.

attrs.location: East Cavalry Field (3 miles east of Gettysburg)
attrs.text: EAST CAVALRY FIELD. Stuart's cavalry (Hampton, Fitz Lee, Chambliss) attacks east of Gettysburg attempting to reach the Union rear during the main assault. Gregg and Custer's Michigan Brigade block the advance.

records.label: East Cavalry Field
records.place: East Cavalry Field (3 miles east of Gettysburg)
records.title: East Cavalry Field

attrs.text: CUSTER'S CHARGE. Custer personally leads the Michigan Brigade in a mounted charge shouting 'Come on you Wolverines!' The charge stops Stuart's advance. Hampton wounded in melee — sabre cut to head.

Stuart's cavalry repulsed at East Cavalry Field. The Confederate cavalry's last chance to reach the Union rear during Pickett's Charge is gone. Pennington's Union horse artillery fires in support throughout.

records.label: Stuart's cavalry repulsed at East Cavalry Field.
records.title: Stuart's cavalry repulsed at East Cavalry Field.

attrs.text: KILPATRICK'S CHARGE. Kilpatrick orders Farnsworth's cavalry brigade to charge Confederate infantry south of the battlefield. Farnsworth protests: the charge is suicidal over rocky terrain against formed infantry.
FARNSWORTH KIA. Farnsworth leads the doomed charge and is killed — a general for only four days. The charge accomplishes nothing. Kilpatrick's decision is universally condemned.

attrs.narrative: Meade's failure to counterattack after Pickett's repulse is his most criticized decision of the battle.
attrs.text: Meade considers a counterattack. Hancock (wounded) urges one. Meade decides the army is too disorganized and depleted. The counterattack that might have destroyed Lee's army does not happen.
Lee begins organizing his army for defense — expecting Meade's counterattack. When it doesn't come, Lee begins considering withdrawal. Ewell, Hill, and Longstreet ordered to consolidate.

records.label: Lee begins organizing his army for defense — expecting Meade's counterattack.
records.title: Lee begins organizing his army for defense — expecting Meade's counterattack.

attrs.text: Both armies largely stationary. Union troops bury the dead and collect wounded. Confederate artillery conserves remaining ammunition. Lee confers with his corps commanders about the retreat.

attrs.narrative: Imboden described Lee at this moment: 'I never saw a man so agitated in my life' — pacing back and forth, saying over and over 'Too bad. Too bad. Oh, too bad.'
attrs.text: Lee orders the retreat to begin on July 4. Imboden's cavalry will escort the enormous wagon train of wounded — 17 miles long. Lee takes full responsibility for the defeat.

records.label: Lee orders the retreat to begin on July 4.
records.title: Lee orders the retreat to begin on July 4.

attrs.text: Rain begins. Both armies exhausted. The Battle of Gettysburg is effectively over. Union casualties: approximately 23,000. Confederate casualties: approximately 28,000. Total: ~51,000 in three days.

attrs.narrative: Gettysburg, combined with Vicksburg's fall on July 4, marks the turning point of the Civil War. The Confederacy would fight on for nearly two more years but the strategic initiative passed permanently to the Union.
attrs.text: END OF THE BATTLE. Total Confederate losses approximately 37% of the army engaged. Total Union losses approximately 25%. The Confederate Army of Northern Virginia will never again mount a strategic offensive into the North. The High Water Mark of the Confederacy has passed.
